about.title: Two Worlds, One Vision
about.quote: Conservation without technology moves too slowly; technology without purpose is hollow. Together, they safeguard life on Earth.
about.bio: I am Morteza Pourmirzai, a wildlife conservation practitioner and founder of Sarvin Wildlife Conservation Institute. My primary dedication is preserving threatened feline species—particularly the Asiatic cheetah—alongside the strategic management and ecological restoration of natural habitats across Iran. Before founding Sarvin, I served as CEO of the Iranian Cheetah Society, spearheading multi-sector initiatives spanning field research, educational advocacy, and ranger support.
about.bio2: Beyond the arid steppe and mountain corridors, I engineer digital infrastructure, optimize high-traffic web systems, configure resilient Linux server clusters, and deploy automated pipelines. I believe transformative nature conservation emerges when rigorous science, ethical human collaboration, and modern software architecture unite.

timeline.text: Initiated ecological field studies and volunteer conservation initiatives across central Iran.
Directed national educational and public awareness campaigns with the Iranian Cheetah Society.
Appointed CEO of the Iranian Cheetah Society; spearheaded large-scale habitat restoration and camera-trap monitoring.
Founded Sarvin Wildlife Conservation Institute to pioneer sustainable wildlife stewardship and technology integration.
